description: Hand-picked car-A/car-B pairs with an expert-judged expected similarity label, used to sanity-check whether DINOv2/CLIP visual-embedding ranking matches what an automotive-design eye would expect. Each 'car' string is resolved to a generation_id via fuzzy match against brand name + model name + code_name (see run_similarity_eval.py) — it is NOT a DB key.

pairs.reason: Direct same-lineage generational succession; should be near the top of each other's similarity list.
Same brand, shared silhouette cues and design language despite different platform.
Shared VW Group MLB Evo platform plus convergent SUV-coupe styling — the app's own 'hidden connection' use case.
Same MLB Evo platform family as the Urus pair, different brand design language layered on top.
Literally co-developed on the same platform by BMW and Toyota — should rank very high.
Competing roadsters, NOT platform-shared — tests whether embeddings catch segment/silhouette convergence without an engineering link.
Same brand family design language (floating roof, minimal shutlines) across adjacent segments.
Same brand DNA (singleframe grille) but very different segment/silhouette (compact coupe vs. mid-engine supercar) — checks embeddings don't over-weight brand grille cues alone.
Shared front-end design language and related platform (Y is a raised/wagon derivative of 3).
American muscle-car competitor convergence on unrelated platforms — classic 'independently arrived at similar design' case.
Sanity floor: unrelated segments, unrelated brands, unrelated everything.
Sanity floor within the same brand — same badge, nothing else in common.
Direct hybrid-supercar competitor convergence — similar proportions and mid-engine packaging despite unrelated platforms.
The SUV-coupe body style itself is a direct competitive response between these two brands.
Same MQB platform, shared proportions and switchgear-era design language.

Deliberately uncertain/borderline case: retro-styling cues are meant to evoke the original, but the actual silhouette and proportions are very different — worth watching whether embeddings over- or under-rate the homage.
Retro-revival competitor convergence — both deliberately references a 1960s-70s small-car silhouette.
Sanity floor within the same brand across a huge era gap.
